fact: 1913年10月10日，美国总统伍德罗·威尔逊在华盛顿按下电钮，经电报引爆巴拿马甘博亚堤（Gamboa Dike），库莱布拉切通的最后一处土石屏障被炸开，加通湖水灌入切通。由于切通内仍有滑坡体，运河此时并未全线通航，此后又疏浚近两个月才打通该段。

sources.title: Panama Canal Authority, Panama Canal Commemorates 100 Years of Dredging Culebra Cut（2013-12-11）
sources.quote: Although October 10, 1913 marked the blast of the Gamboa Dike which removed the last land barrier and joined Culebra Cut and Gatun Lake, the Panama Canal was not fully navigable due to landslides in Culebra Cut. It was necessary to continue dredging for nearly two months to complete the opening of this stretch.

sources.title: HISTORIC AMERICAN BUILDINGS SURVEY, Fort Sherman（HABS No. CZ-6）
sources.quote: On 10 October, President Woodrow Wilson pressed a button in Washington that carried to Panama to blow up the Gamboa Dike and fill the Culebra Cut.

fact: 1913年夏，运河的船闸与库莱布拉切通均已完工；9月26日在加通船闸首次放水。船闸工程1909年开工，历时约四年，闸室墙长1000英尺、高80英尺，共六对闸室以通行双线船队。

sources.title: HISTORIC AMERICAN BUILDINGS SURVEY, Fort Sherman（HABS No. CZ-6）
sources.quote: Work on the locks began in 1909 and took about four years. The bases of the lock chambers were concrete, with steel gates. The walls were a thousand feet long and eighty feet high. Six pairs of chambers were built (to handle two lanes of traffic). ... By the summer of 1913, the locks and the Cut were finished. On 26 September at Gatun, water was first turned into the locks.

fact: 1913年之后运河才真正通航：1914年1月7日，浮吊「亚历山大·拉瓦莱」号成为第一艘自航跨越两大洋的船只；1914年8月3日客货船「克里斯托瓦尔」号首次完整通过；1914年8月15日运河正式通航，货船「安孔」号通过。1904年至通航，工程花费约3.52亿美元，5,609名工人死亡。

sources.title: HISTORIC AMERICAN BUILDINGS SURVEY, Fort Sherman（HABS No. CZ-6）
sources.quote: On 15 August, in a small ceremony, the Canal opened when the ship Ancon successfully passed through. From 1904 to its opening, the Canal had cost $352 million, and 5,609 workers died.

sources.title: Panama Canal（Wikipedia 镜像页，述首航船只与日期）
sources.quote: Alexandre La Valley (a floating crane built by Lobnitz & Company and launched in 1887) was the first self-propelled vessel to transit the canal from ocean to ocean. This vessel crossed the canal from the Atlantic in stages during construction, finally reaching the Pacific on 7 January 1914. SS Cristobal ... on 3 August 1914, was the first ship to transit the canal from ocean to ocean.

fact: 运河区的用工被分为「金册」（gold roll）与「银册」（silver roll）两类，名义上按技能划分，实际按种族划分：金册以美国白人技工与管理层为主，按美元金币发薪；银册以加勒比海黑人劳工为主，按当地银币发薪。1908年战争部长塔夫脱下令金册限于美国与巴拿马公民，黑人美国公民虽可上榜但无金册待遇，1909年后运河区几乎不再雇用黑人美国人。两类的住房、食堂、娱乐、医疗乃至邮局窗口均分开。

sources.title: Gold roll（Wikipedia 镜像页）
sources.quote: The gold roll and the silver roll were racially coded payroll categories of workers employed by the U.S. builders of the Panama Canal. ... The gold roll was explicitly limited to U.S. and Panamanian citizens by order of U.S. Secretary of War William Howard Taft during his 1908 presidential campaign ... A small number of black American citizens were also employed on the gold roll but were denied gold roll privileges. In response to their protests, the canal authorities stopped hiring black U.S. citizens. Hardly any black American citizens remained on the canal workforce after 1909.

sources.title: Linda Hall Library, The Land Divided, The World United: Life in the Zone
sources.quote: The system was originally intended to designate skilled and unskilled labor but quickly grew into a system of segregation. Gold payroll workers were white, primarily American, more highly paid, and paid in U.S. gold coin. The silver payroll workers, mainly from the Caribbean islands ... were paid much less and in Panamanian silver coin. The system was a color line, with separate privileges, eating facilities, and building entrances for gold and silver workers.

fact: 运河区银册劳工的工资约为每小时10美分、每天10小时、每周6天，约为金册白人或欧洲工人工资的一半；银册工人住无隔断的集体工棚，在无座位、无遮棚的露天食堂就餐，不能使用减价 commissary（内部商店）、游泳池与电影院；金册工人则有独立住宅、室内食堂与全套福利。1906年上半年，非白人死亡率约千分之五十九，白人约千分之十七。

sources.title: Hektoen International, Death, disease, and discrimination during the construction of the Panama Canal (1904–1914)
sources.quote: Skilled white laborers were paid in U.S. dollars (“gold roll”), while non-white unskilled workers were paid in Colombian pesos (“silver roll”), which were equivalent to only half of the gold roll wages. Wages were ten cents an hour for ten hours a day, six days a week. ... Amenities such as movies, pool parlors, swimming pools, and access to commissaries for cheaper clothing and food were not permitted for silver-roll personnel. ... for the first semester of 1906, death rates were fifty-nine per thousand for non-whites compared to only seventeen per thousand for white employees.

sources.title: Stanford CLAS, Teacher's Guide: Silver People: Voices from the Panama Canal
sources.quote: Those on the Silver Roll, the unskilled workers, were paid in balboas, or local Panamanian silver. West Indian workers, plentiful in numbers and eager to work, could be paid 10 cents an hour—half of the salary of a European or white U.S. worker.

fact: 巴拿马运河的工程造价约3.52亿美元（1904年至通航），美国另因巴拿马独立争端同意向哥伦比亚支付2500万美元；通航后普通货运通行费为每货运吨90美分。到1924年，运河年通行船舶超过5000艘。

sources.title: HISTORIC AMERICAN BUILDINGS SURVEY, Fort Sherman（HABS No. CZ-6）
sources.quote: From 1904 to its opening, the Canal had cost $352 million ... The United States also agreed to pay Colombia $25 million over disputes from the Panama Revolution ... Normal tolls for the Canal were ninety cents per cargo ton. ... by 1924, the Canal was handling more than five thousand ships per year.

fact: 巴拿马运河采用船闸式高水位方案：船只经三级船闸从海平面升至高于海平面约85英尺的加通湖，再经库莱布拉切通下降至另一侧海面；加通坝蓄水形成当时世界最大的人工湖。1913年10月甘博亚堤爆破后，切通与加通湖连通，但切通内的库库拉查滑坡（Cucuracha Slide）仍阻断航道，需持续疏浚。

sources.title: Through the Grand Canyon from Wyoming to Mexico（1920年代记述，述船闸与湖面高程）
sources.quote: The surface of the Gatun Lake at this time was over sixty feet above sea-level. ... the demolition of the Gamboa Dike only joined two bodies of fresh water, which had come from the same source-the Chagres River. ... Each ocean is joined, by means of three great locks, to a large inland lake of fresh water- eighty-five feet above their level.

sources.title: HISTORIC AMERICAN BUILDINGS SURVEY, Fort Sherman（HABS No. CZ-6）
sources.quote: This act also marked the final stage in the creation of Lake Gatun, the largest man-made lake at that time.
